# Gold V1 — H1 data-quality gate

**Result: DATA QUALITY PASS** (machine record: `data_quality.json`, regenerated by `h1_study.py` on every run; the study
aborts if any check fails).

Input: `data/exness/gold/phase2a/raw/xauusd_XAUUSDm_M15.csv` (Exness XAUUSDm, MT5 CopyRates, bid prices). The loader
cuts at 2026-06-03 00:00 UTC **before** any computation. Development rows: 10,355 M15 bars, 2025-12-23 00:00 →
2026-06-02 23:45 UTC.

| # | check | result | evidence / method |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Continuity (excluding weekends, daily closure, holidays) | PASS | 113 gaps > 15 min, all explained. 85 daily breaks of 75 min (84) or 90 min (1, 2026-03-08 DST changeover). 22 weekend gaps. 6 holiday/early-close gaps: Christmas (12-24 18:15 → 12-25 23:00), New Year (12-31 → 01-01 23:00), MLK (01-19 early close 19:15), Presidents Day (02-16 19:15), Good Friday (04-02 20:45 → 04-05 22:00), Memorial Day (05-25 18:15). No missing bars inside sessions: 107 trading days have the full 92 bars; the short days are the holiday/DST days above. |
| 2 | UTC timestamps | PASS | The daily break falls at 17:00 America/New_York in both regimes: last bar 21:45 UTC / reopen 23:00 UTC under EST, last bar 20:45 UTC / reopen 22:00 UTC from 2026-03-08 (EDT). Only UTC timestamps are consistent with a New-York-anchored broker day across the DST change. |
| 3 | London DST | PASS | Sessions are built with `zoneinfo` (Europe/London): 08:00 London = 08:00 UTC in January and 07:00 UTC in May (BST from 2026-03-29). |
| 4 | New York DST | PASS | `zoneinfo` America/New_York: 08:00 NY = 13:00 UTC in January, 12:00 UTC in May (EDT from 2026-03-08). The broker's own break moves with it (check 2). |
| 5 | Session boundaries | PASS | Asia 00:00–07:00 UTC; London 08:00–16:30 Europe/London; New York 08:00–17:00 America/New_York; Overlap = both open; everything else Other. Boundary cases asserted (07:45 UTC Jan = Other, 08:00 Jan = London, 07:00 May = London, 13:00 Jan = Overlap, 20:45 May = New York, 03:00 = Asia). |
| 6 | TVWAP daily/session reset | PASS | Reset on the first bar after the daily break (the broker trading day, which starts 22:00/23:00 UTC). The first bar's TVWAP equals its typical price on every checked day. |
| 7 | TVWAP calculation | PASS | Weighted mean and weighted population variance of typical price (H+L+C)/3 with tick-volume weights; ±1σ/±2σ = TVWAP ± k·σ. Independent naive `np.average` recomputation on every 9th trading day agrees to < 1e-7. The first implementation used E[x²] − m², which lost ~6e-5 of σ precision at a price of ~4000; the gate caught it, and the variance is now accumulated relative to the day's first typical price. |
| 8 | PDH/PDL use completed previous days only | PASS | PDH/PDL = high/low of the previous broker trading day, joined by trading-day id; asserted equal to the previous day's aggregate for every day. |
| 9 | Asia range frozen after Asia ends | PASS | The Asia high/low is NaN on every bar before 07:00 UTC **and** on the pre-Asia bars of the trading day (22:00–23:59 UTC). The first implementation exposed that day's future Asia range to those evening bars; the prefix-invariance test caught this real leak and it was fixed. After Asia, one value per day. |
| 10 | No future leak in swing/sweep logic | PASS | Prefix invariance: features recomputed on the first 70% of rows equal the full-run features on that prefix (ATR, TVWAP, σ, Asia range, PDH, ER, ATR percentile, range percentile, volume ratio), and every full-run event whose entry lies inside the prefix is also detected on the prefix alone. H1 context uses the previous completed hour only; percentiles use strictly earlier bars. |
| 11 | Spread field alignment | PASS, semantics UNRESOLVED | MetaQuotes does not document whether `MqlRates.spread` is the open, close, minimum or average spread. Values are quantised (most common: 280, 160, 240, 360 points; point = 0.001); the median is flat at 280 across hours except 21 UTC, the minimum is 160 in every hour, and the correlation with bar range is −0.04. This pattern suggests a minimum or snapshot spread rather than a maximum. It is used only as a descriptive spread/risk ratio; no conclusion depends on it. Treat it as a lower bound. |
| 12 | Intrabar ordering ambiguity | PASS | M15 OHLC cannot order the high and the low. The forward race marks a target and −1R reached in the same bar as `ambiguous` (AMBIGUOUS_INTRABAR). These are reported separately and excluded from the P(...) figures, with a conservative variant counting them as losses (`p*R_cons` in `summary()`). 1 of 102 events and 9 of 510 controls are ambiguous at some target. |

Also noted: `real_volume` is always 0, so tick volume is the only participation measure and TVWAP is a
tick-volume proxy, not a traded-volume VWAP.
